_about: Anís request types, one research strategy each (planning/anis-question-scenarios-20261102.html). A question may need several: lead + also. Follow-up moves (G*) apply to messages that depend on the thread.

types.A1: A fact: a date, author, number, place or other single checkable fact
types.A2: Find a book or text by its name, or ask to read/download it
types.A3: Find passages on a topic (show me what the texts say about X; quotes about X; a bare topic)
types.A4: A quotation: who said it, where it comes from, is it authentic, what are the exact words
types.A5: Look up a reference (chapter and verse, a numbered paragraph, a named tablet section)
types.A6: What a word or term means (a technical term, a name, a foreign word)
types.B1: What a tradition or figure teaches or believes about a topic
types.B2: Explain a specific passage the reader is reading or quotes
types.B3: Why or how: the reason for a teaching, how something works
types.B4: Tell a story or historical event
types.C1: Two or more named traditions compared on one topic
types.C2: X vs Y head to head (two concepts, works, people, practices, or two religions as a whole)
types.C3: What all or most religions say about a topic
types.C4: Two accounts, editions or translations of the same thing compared
types.D1: Personal grief, fear, doubt or struggle: wants comfort or meaning
types.D2: A prayer for an occasion or need
types.D3: Religious law, rules and personal practice (fasting, diet, marriage, burial, alcohol, rituals)
types.D4: Community life and service (Fund, elections, Feast, study circles, junior youth, plans, institutions)
types.D5: Joining or leaving: is it a cult, how to convert, should I join, can I belong to two
types.E2: Asks for something that may not exist or a false premise
types.E3: A controversial or sensitive topic (sexuality, gender roles, schism, violence, criticism)
types.F1: Compile quotations or passages on a theme (a collection, not one answer)
types.F2: Prepare a devotional program or reading for an occasion
types.F3: Prepare a study session, lesson, talk or class
types.F4: Make a timeline, chart, table, map or visual
types.F5: A research brief or long written report
types.F6: Teach me over time: a reading plan or course
types.G1: Follow-up: refers back to something in the last reply (that one, the second passage)
types.G2: Follow-up: asks for the source of what was said
types.G3: Follow-up: asks for the exact words
types.G4: Follow-up: go deeper on something already discussed
types.G5: Follow-up: compare what was discussed with another tradition or text
types.G6: Follow-up: pushes back on the last answer
types.G7: Follow-up: reshape the last answer (shorter, simpler, another language, email it)
types.H1: About Anís or the library itself, greeting or small talk
types.H2: Vague opener or bare word where the intent cannot be told
